_notes: FULL-COVERAGE DUMMY 1099-R — all 73 writable boxes on Drake's 1099 screen carry a
value, so one run proves the whole map at once. Nothing on this screen is a
'<Click to Access>' sub-screen, so unlike the INT and DIV screens there is no box that
has to be left out.
The amounts are deliberately distinct and nothing like a real statement — 1000, 1100,
1200 ... — so every box on the screenshot can be traced back to the field that wrote
it. This is a TEST RETURN payload. It is not anybody's tax data.
FIELD 1 IS TS, NOT TSJ. Drake offers T and S only on this screen — a pension belongs to
one person. Sending 'J' here is refused by the map before Drake is opened.
BOX 7 IS TWO BOXES. The distribution code is fields 33 and 34, each a separate
single-character dropdown. 'box7_dist_code' below is sent as '1B' ON PURPOSE, to prove
the split: the plan should show field 33 = '1' and field 34 = 'B'. A dropped second
character is a wrong tax, not a cosmetic loss — code 1 alone means an early
distribution with no known exception, and the 10% penalty rides on it.
FIELDS 16-24 ARE OVERRIDE BOXES for the recipient's name and address. A value there
REPLACES what the return already holds from screen 1. They are filled here because the
job of this payload is to prove every box can be written; on a real return they should
be left alone unless the document's address genuinely differs.
The amount/percent pairs (36/37, 70/71, 72/73) are alternatives — Drake expects one or
the other on each row. Both are sent here for coverage. No real return should be sent
this way.
pension_type is 'G' (US Government). Drake offers 44 codes and SEVEN of them are
symbols (@ # * % & $ =) for AZ, CT, PA, NY and MD. It also lists 'Z' twice, so the code
alone does not identify the entry — check it by eye.
ALL THIRTEEN DROPDOWNS ARE NOW CONFIRMED — the live run on 2026-08-14 read every one of
them back off the form, including both halves of Box 7. They still carry the
verify-by-eye flag: a dropdown with no matching entry accepts the typing, echoes it in
the heads-down popup and stores NOTHING, so the per-field gate can pass while the box
stays empty, and only the form check catches that.
The second state row is OHIO on purpose. It was NJ, and the locality box would not
fill: New Jersey levies no local income tax that Drake tracks, so that dropdown is
genuinely EMPTY and there is nothing to select in it, by robot or by hand. Ohio has
real city income taxes, so the row can actually be proven.
Client: the test return 123456789 / fynn, Test.
